metadata.title: Reddit stock jumps after S&P 500 inclusion announcement

content.text:
Reddit will join the S&P 500 on Aug. 18, replacing AvalonBay Communities, S&P Dow Jones Indices announced Thursday. Reddit stock climbed 12.6% in after-hours trading following the announcement.
Reddit will take AvalonBay's slot in the Communication Services sector. AvalonBay is being acquired by fellow S&P 500 member Equity Residential in a deal expected to close soon, pending final conditions. The combined company will be renamed Vivmark Residential and will remain in the S&P 500, according to S&P Dow Jones Indices.
Reddit becomes only the second pureplay social media company in the S&P 500, according to CNBC. Meta is the other. Pinterest and Snap, though earlier to go public, have not grown to Reddit's scale by market capitalization. Twitter had been an S&P 500 constituent before Elon Musk's 2022 takeover; the platform was subsequently rebranded as X and operates under SpaceX ownership.
When a stock enters a major index, it typically gets a lift from institutional investors who must adjust their portfolios to mirror the new composition, driving up demand for newly added shares.
Reddit posted first-quarter revenue of $663 million, a 69% increase from a year earlier, with advertising accounting for the bulk of that growth. The company has now recorded eight straight quarters of sales growth exceeding 60%, according to CNBC. Reddit's second-quarter results, reported in late July, drew concern from investors after CEO Steve Huffman told analysts that "search referrals were choppy," raising questions about the company's reliance on Google for new users. Huffman pointed to Google's aggressive rollout of its Gemini-powered AI Overviews as the force behind the uneven referral traffic. Reddit stock fell following those results.
As part of the same round of index changes, Sun Communities will join the S&P MidCap 400 on Aug. 20, replacing Webster Financial, which is being acquired by Banco Santander, according to S&P Dow Jones Indices.
